q: What does a web server send back to your browser?
options: A picture of the finished page
A block of text the browser interprets
why: The server sends text - HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Everything you see is the browser's interpretation of that text.

q: Which is NOT part of the World Wide Web?
why: WhatsApp uses the internet but is not the web. The web is pages and links carried over the internet.

q: What does HTTP stand for?
why: HTTP is the request-response protocol the browser and server speak.

q: The statement 'HTTP is stateless' means:
options: The server does not remember you between requests
Only one user can connect at a time
why: Each request is independent. Cookies and tokens exist precisely to work around this.

q: In the client-server model, your browser is the:
why: The client asks; the server stores and sends.

q: Which three languages make up the front end of a page?
why: HTML is structure, CSS is presentation, JavaScript is behaviour.

q: Anything you send to a browser can be read by the user. What does this mean for security?
options: You can hide a password in JavaScript
Nothing sent to the browser is secret
why: View Source and DevTools expose everything. Secrets must stay on the server.

q: Which declaration must appear at the very top of an HTML5 page?
why: <!DOCTYPE html> tells the browser to use modern standards mode.

q: What happens if you omit the doctype?
why: Quirks mode applies 1990s rules; the page usually renders but spacing and box sizes shift, which is a painful bug to trace.

q: Which section holds information ABOUT the page rather than visible content?
why: <head> holds metadata. <header> is visible content - do not confuse the two.

q: What is the difference between <head> and <header>?
options: head holds metadata; header is visible page content
header holds metadata; head is visible
why: This pair is examined constantly. head is invisible metadata; header is a visible landmark inside body.

q: Which attribute declares the page's language?
why: <html lang="en"> helps screen readers pronounce the content.

q: What does <meta charset="UTF-8"> do?
why: Without it, accented characters and symbols such as the rupee sign render as junk.

q: Which meta tag is essential for a page to work properly on phones?
why: Without viewport, a phone pretends to be a 980px desktop and shrinks the page to unreadable size.

q: Which tag's content appears on the browser tab AND as the headline in search results?
why: <title> supplies both. The description meta tag supplies the grey summary underneath.

q: What is the correct order of the main structural elements?
why: head and body are siblings inside html; head comes first.

q: Which of these is a valid, complete minimal HTML5 document?
why: A complete document needs doctype, html with lang, head with charset and title, and body.

q: In <p class="intro">Hello</p>, what is 'class="intro"'?
why: Attributes give extra information and always live in the OPENING tag.

q: How many ELEMENTS are in <p>Hi <b>there</b></p>?
why: A paragraph element, with a bold element nested inside it.

q: Which of these is an empty (void) element?
why: <br> has no content, so it never gets a closing tag.

q: Which is written INCORRECTLY?
why: Empty elements have nothing to close, so </br> is invalid.

q: Which nesting is correct?
why: Whatever opens last must close first, exactly like brackets.

q: Why is <div class=my box> a problem?
options: Unquoted values break at the space, creating two attributes
why: Without quotes the browser reads class="my" and a separate attribute 'box'. Always quote attribute values.

q: Which attribute must be UNIQUE on a page?
why: Duplicate ids do not stop rendering, which is what makes them dangerous - links and scripts only ever find the first.

q: Two elements both have id="main". What breaks?
options: Fragment links and scripts only find the first one
why: It fails silently, which is far harder to debug than an error.

q: How many heading levels does HTML provide?
why: Six levels, h1 through h6. They describe the document outline, not the font size.

q: How many <h1> elements should a page normally have?
why: One h1 states the page's single subject; further sections use h2.

q: You want a subheading smaller than h2. What is correct?
options: Skip to h5 because it renders smaller
Use h3 and set the size in CSS
why: Heading level describes position in the outline; appearance is CSS's job.

q: What is the correct use of <br>?
options: To break a line inside a single block of text
why: br is for a line break WITHIN one idea - an address, a verse. Separate ideas need separate <p> elements.

q: Why is <br><br> between two ideas poor practice?
options: A screen reader announces one run-on paragraph
why: It also makes spacing unadjustable without editing HTML. Spacing is CSS's job.

q: What does <hr> represent semantically?
options: A thematic break - the subject changes
why: Drawing a line is a side effect; the meaning is a change of topic.

q: You type ten spaces between two words in a <p>. How many appear on screen?
why: HTML collapses consecutive whitespace to a single space, unless the text is inside <pre>.

q: Which pair is SEMANTIC rather than purely presentational?
why: strong means importance and em means emphasis; b and i only change appearance.

q: You want to mark a genuine safety warning. Which tag?
why: strong conveys importance to screen readers; b merely looks bold.

q: When is <i> the correct choice over <em>?
options: For a different KIND of text such as a species name or foreign phrase
why: em changes the sentence's meaning; i marks text that differs in kind.

q: Which tag highlights text like a marker pen?
why: <mark> renders with a highlight by default.

q: Which pair marks removed and inserted text?
why: Useful for showing an old price struck through and a new one inserted.

q: How do you write H₂O correctly in HTML?
why: sub lowers text; sup raises it.

q: Which element preserves your exact spaces and line breaks?
why: <pre> is the only one that does not collapse whitespace.

q: What is wrong with <q>"a decisive shift"</q>?
options: The quote marks are typed manually
why: The browser adds quotation marks automatically, so typing them gives you two sets.

q: What does the <cite> ELEMENT mark up?
options: The title of a creative work
why: The cite ELEMENT holds a work's title. The cite ATTRIBUTE on q or blockquote holds a URL. This distinction is examined often.

q: Which is used for a LONG quotation as its own block?
why: q is inline and short; blockquote is a block.

q: How do you write an HTML comment?
why: Comments are invisible on the page but fully visible in View Source.

q: A page renders normally then goes blank halfway down. What is the most likely cause?
why: Everything after an unclosed comment is swallowed.

q: Which element marks contact details for a page or article?
why: <address> is for contact details, not any postal address that happens to appear in the text.

q: Which tag marks up an abbreviation with its full form?
why: The title attribute holds the expansion and shows as a tooltip.

q: Which tag creates a NUMBERED list?
why: ol = ordered. Use it when order matters.

q: Which element defines a term inside a <dl>?
why: dt is the term; dd is its description.

q: Which elements may sit DIRECTLY inside a <ul>?
why: Loose text or other elements placed directly inside a list are invalid.

q: Where must a nested list be placed?
options: Inside an <li> of the parent list
why: The sub-list describes ONE item, so it belongs inside that item's li, before the closing </li>.

q: Which attribute makes an ordered list start at 5?
why: <ol start="5">.

q: <ol type="a"> produces markers that look like:
why: Lowercase type="a" gives lowercase letters; type="A" gives capitals.

q: Why mark a navigation menu as a list even though CSS removes the bullets?
options: So a screen reader announces the item count
why: A screen-reader user hears 'list, 5 items' and knows how many options there are. Loose links tell them nothing.

q: Which attribute holds a link's destination?
why: href on <a>. src is for embedded resources such as images.

q: <a href="#contact"> will do nothing unless:
why: A fragment link needs a matching id, or the click silently does nothing.

q: Which opens a link in a new tab?
why: target="_blank" - and pair it with rel="noopener".

q: Why add rel="noopener" to a target="_blank" link?
options: It stops the new page scripting your tab
It is required for the link to work
why: Without it the opened page can reach back through window.opener and replace your tab with a fake login page.

q: Which attribute describes an image for screen readers?
why: alt is read aloud and displayed if the image fails to load.

q: What is the correct alt text for a purely decorative image?
why: An empty but PRESENT alt tells a screen reader to skip it silently.

q: How do you make an image clickable?
why: <a href="..."><img ...></a>

q: Why set width and height on an <img>?
options: It reserves space so the page does not jump
why: Without them the layout shifts as each image loads.

q: Which pair marks up an illustration with its caption?
why: figure wraps the illustration; figcaption is its caption.

q: Your site works locally but every link breaks on GitHub Pages. What is the most likely cause?
options: GitHub Pages does not support links
Wrong relative paths, or capitalisation - the server is case-sensitive
why: Windows ignores case; the web server does not. About.html and about.html are different files there.

q: What does SVG stand for?
why: Scalable Vector Graphics - it stores instructions, not pixels.

q: Why does an SVG stay sharp when enlarged?
options: It stores drawing instructions, not a pixel grid
why: The browser re-draws the shapes at whatever size is needed.

q: Which attribute defines an SVG's internal coordinate system?
why: viewBox sets the coordinate space; width and height set the rendered size.

q: In SVG, which way does the y axis grow?
why: Screen coordinates, not graph paper. Increasing y moves DOWN.

q: Which attributes position a <circle>?
why: cx, cy for the centre and r for the radius.

q: How do you give an inline <svg> an accessible description?
why: alt exists only on img, area and input. SVG uses role and aria-label.

q: A <line> renders as nothing. What is missing?
why: A line has no area to fill; it needs a stroke to be visible.

q: Your shape uses coordinates near 500 but viewBox is "0 0 100 100". What happens?
options: It is clipped and appears to vanish
why: Anything outside the viewBox range is simply not drawn.

q: Which attribute shows play, pause and volume on a video?
why: Without controls there is no way for the visitor to start playback.

q: What does controls="false" do on a <video>?
why: controls is BOOLEAN - the browser only checks whether it is present. To hide controls, remove the attribute entirely.

q: Why does autoplay often not work without muted?
options: Browsers block sound that starts on its own
why: Unexpected noise is hostile, so browsers permit autoplay only when muted.

q: Why give a <video> several <source> elements?
options: So the browser picks the first format it supports
why: mp4 plus webm covers essentially every browser.

q: Which attribute shows a still image before a video plays?
why: poster="cover.jpg".

q: Which element embeds another web page inside the current one?
why: <iframe> embeds a whole separate document.

q: Which attribute must every <iframe> have for accessibility?
why: Without title, a screen reader announces only 'frame'.

q: Your iframe stays blank when embedding a large website. Why?
options: The remote site forbids being embedded
why: Many sites send a header refusing to be framed. That is their choice, not your bug.

q: What does loading="lazy" do?
options: Delays loading until it is nearly on screen
why: A genuine performance win on long pages.

q: Which element is NOT an empty element?
why: <video> always needs a closing tag, even when you use src.

q: Which tag's content becomes the clickable blue headline in search results?
why: title supplies the headline; the description meta supplies the grey summary beneath it.

q: Does stuffing keywords into <meta name="keywords"> improve Google ranking?
options: No - Google has ignored it since 2009
why: It is on the syllabus so you must know it exists, but it has no SEO value today.

q: Which link text is better for SEO and accessibility?
why: Link text should describe the destination. A screen-reader user listing links hears 'here, here, here' otherwise.

q: What is robots.txt?
options: A file at the site root asking crawlers which paths to skip
why: It is a REQUEST, not security - and it is publicly readable.

q: Why is listing an admin path in robots.txt a bad idea?
options: robots.txt is public, so you advertise the path
why: Well-behaved crawlers obey it; malicious ones read it as a list of interesting places to look.

q: Which tool checks your HTML for structural errors?
why: It catches unclosed tags, duplicate ids and bad nesting - exactly the bugs that fail silently.

q: Why is HTML failing SILENTLY a problem?
options: There is no error message, so bugs survive
why: The page 'looks fine on my laptop' and breaks elsewhere.

q: Which is the recommended way to attach CSS to a real project?
why: One file styles every page and the browser caches it.

q: Which is BAD practice in modern HTML?
why: Tables are for data, not layout.

q: How should tags and attributes be written?
why: HTML tolerates uppercase, but every style guide requires lowercase.

q: Which practice most improves BOTH SEO and accessibility?
options: Descriptive alt text and link text
why: Good SEO and good accessibility are largely the same work.

q: How many <main> elements may a page contain?
why: main marks the single unique content area of the document.

q: Which test decides between <section> and <article>?
options: Whether the block would still make sense on a different website
why: Self-contained and portable means article. Part of THIS page means section.

q: A blog post that could be republished elsewhere should be marked as:
why: It stands alone, so it is an article.

q: What is the practical benefit of semantic elements over <div>?
options: Screen readers and search engines can understand the structure
They need less CSS to style
why: They render identically. The gain is that the structure becomes machine-readable.

q: A screen-reader user on a page built only from divs must:
options: Listen through the whole menu on every page load
why: Landmarks such as <main> let them jump straight to the content.

q: Which element holds content that is related but not essential?
why: A sidebar, a pull quote, a related-links box.

q: Can <footer> appear inside an <article>?
options: Yes - it can close a section or article
why: An article can have its own header and footer, for example a byline.

q: A <section> with no heading usually means:
options: A plain <div> was the right choice
why: A section should own a heading; if there is no natural one, it is not really a section.

q: Which is the correct nesting order?
why: nav sits inside header; section sits inside main.

q: Which of these is an INLINE element by default?
why: span flows inside the text without breaking the line.

q: Which of these is a BLOCK element by default?
why: A block takes the full line and starts a new one.

q: Which is VALID?
why: Inline elements go inside block elements, not the other way round.

q: You set width:200px on a <span> and nothing happens. Why?
options: Inline elements ignore width and height
why: Use display:inline-block or make it a block to give it a width.

q: What happens with <p><div>text</div></p>?
options: The paragraph auto-closes before the div
why: You end up with an empty p and stray text - a confusing bug to trace.

q: Which element gives a table its title?
why: <caption> must be the FIRST child of <table>.

q: Where must <caption> be placed?
why: Anywhere else is invalid and may not render.

q: Which attribute merges a cell ACROSS columns?
why: colspan stretches sideways; rowspan stretches downwards.

q: A 4-column table has a row containing a cell with colspan="3". How many cell tags does that row need in total?
why: The spanning cell covers three columns, so only one more cell is needed - two tags in total.

q: A cell has rowspan="2". What must the NEXT row do?
options: Omit one cell in that column
why: The spanning cell already occupies that column in the next row.

q: What is the difference between <th> and <td>?
options: th is bold, td is not
th is a HEADER cell that describes what its row or column means
th can only appear in thead
why: Bold and centred is only the default styling; the meaning is the point.

q: What does scope="row" do?
options: Tells assistive tech this header describes its row
why: With th and scope, a screen reader announces 'Monday, Time, 9am' rather than just '9am'.

q: Which is INVALID?
why: A cell must sit inside a <tr>, never directly inside <table>.

q: Which element groups the summary or total rows?
why: thead, tbody and tfoot group the three parts of a table.

q: Which attribute on <label> ties it to a field?
why: for must match the input's id exactly.

q: What is the difference between id and name on an input?
options: id links the label; name is the key the value is submitted under
name links the label; id is submitted
why: id is for the browser, name is for the server.

q: Your form submits but one field is missing at the server. What is the likeliest cause?
why: Without name="..." the value is never sent. A very common CA1 bug.

q: A field is filled in but marked disabled. On submit it is:
why: disabled excludes the field from submission. Use readonly if the value must still be sent.

q: Which attribute shows a value that cannot be edited but IS submitted?
why: readonly submits; disabled does not. This pair is examined often.

q: Why is placeholder NOT a substitute for a label?
options: It disappears as soon as the user types
why: Halfway through a long form the user cannot remember what the field wanted.

q: Which element groups related fields and names the group?
why: Essential for radio groups - a screen reader then announces 'Gender: male' rather than just 'male'.

q: Which is written correctly?
why: textarea is not a void element, and its value goes BETWEEN the tags.

q: Which attribute pre-selects an <option>?
why: selected is for option; checked is for radio and checkbox.

q: Which input type hides characters as they are typed?
why: type="password" masks the characters on screen.

q: Which input type makes a phone show an @ key?
why: The type changes the on-screen keyboard as well as the validation.

q: Three radio buttons each have a DIFFERENT name. What happens?
options: All three can be selected at once
why: The shared name is what groups radios. With different names each is its own group of one.

q: Two checkboxes share the same name. Is that valid?
options: Yes - they submit together as a set of values
Only if they have different ids
why: Unlike radios, same-named checkboxes can all be ticked and all submit.

q: Which attribute pre-ticks a checkbox?
why: checked for radio and checkbox; selected for option.

q: Which set of attributes bounds a number input?
why: min, max and step also drive the spinner's increments.

q: Which input type produces a slider?
why: type="range" with min and max.

q: Which input type opens a file chooser?
why: Add multiple to allow more than one file.

q: Which attribute blocks submission while a field is empty?
why: required is a boolean attribute.

q: Can a determined user bypass required and minlength?
options: No, it is enforced by the browser
Yes, trivially - so the server must re-check
why: Client-side validation is for CONVENIENCE, not security. DevTools can remove the attribute.

q: Which pair limits how many CHARACTERS may be typed?
why: min/max bound the VALUE; minlength/maxlength bound the length.

q: Which button type sends the form?
why: type="button" has no built-in behaviour at all.

q: Which is the most accessible way to label a radio button?
options: A <label> using for/id, or wrapping the input
why: Both work; wrapping is neat for radios. Loose text is not associated with the control.

q: In the rule p { color: navy; }, what is 'color: navy'?
why: Property plus value is a declaration; 'p' is the selector.

q: Which selector targets class="card"?
why: A dot for a class, a hash for an id.

q: Which selector targets id="header"?
why: Ids use #. They must be unique on the page.

q: What does 'article p' (with a space) select?
options: Paragraphs that are direct children only
why: The space is a descendant combinator meaning 'somewhere inside'.

q: What is the difference between '.card .wide' and '.card.wide'?
options: With a space: a .wide inside a .card. Without: one element with both classes
why: That single space changes the meaning completely.

q: Which selects only DIRECT children?
why: > is the child combinator, one level down only.

q: Which is the best way to include CSS in a real project?
why: Reusable across pages and cached by the browser.

q: Which wins: '#box p' or '.card .inner .text p'?
why: #box p scores (1,0,1); the other (0,3,1). Compare left to right - one id beats any number of classes.

q: When does source ORDER decide which rule wins?
why: A more specific rule written earlier still beats a later one.

q: Which has the HIGHEST specificity?
why: One id outranks any number of classes or elements.

q: Your CSS rule is being ignored. What should you do FIRST?
options: Count the specificity of the rule beating it
why: !important starts an arms race that makes the stylesheet unmaintainable.

q: Which property is INHERITED by child elements?
why: color, font-family and line-height inherit; box properties do not.

q: Which is the space INSIDE the border?
why: Padding takes the background colour; margin is always transparent.

q: width:200px, padding:20px, border:5px, no box-sizing. How wide is the element?
why: 200 + 20 + 20 + 5 + 5 = 250. With box-sizing:border-box it would be exactly 200.

q: What does box-sizing: border-box do?
options: Makes width include padding and border
why: One line that removes an entire category of sizing bug.

q: In 'padding: 10px 20px', what does 20px apply to?
why: Two values mean top/bottom then left/right.

q: 'padding: 5px 10px 15px 20px' applies 15px to which side?
why: Clockwise from the top: top, right, bottom, left.

q: How do you centre a fixed-width block horizontally?
options: margin: 0 auto with a width set
why: auto splits the leftover space evenly on both sides.

q: Which unit is relative to the ROOT font size?
why: rem is predictable; em compounds relative to the parent.

q: Why prefer rem over px for font sizes?
options: It respects the reader's browser font setting
why: That is an accessibility win - px ignores the user's preference.

q: What does 1vw mean?
why: vh is the same for height.

q: What is the default position value?
why: With static, top/left/right/bottom do nothing.

q: An absolutely positioned box flies to the page corner instead of its parent's. Why?
options: No ancestor has a position other than static
why: absolute measures from the nearest POSITIONED ancestor. Add position:relative to the parent.

q: Which position keeps the element's original space in the flow?
why: relative shifts the element visually but its space is preserved.

q: Which position is measured against the VIEWPORT?
why: fixed stays put while the page scrolls.

q: position: sticky silently does nothing. What is missing?
why: Without an offset such as top:0 it behaves like static.

q: Where do you put display:flex?
why: The children become flex items automatically.

q: Which property spaces items along the MAIN axis?
why: align-items works along the CROSS axis.

q: With flex-direction: column, justify-content now controls:
why: justify-content always follows the MAIN axis, which becomes vertical in a column.

q: Which centres content both horizontally and vertically?
why: Two lines that used to require genuine hacks.

q: Why prefer gap over margins between flex items?
options: gap adds space only BETWEEN items, not at the ends
why: No leftover edge space to cancel out.

q: Cards squash instead of moving to a new line on a phone. What is missing?
why: Without wrap, flex items shrink indefinitely on one line.

q: What does the fr unit mean in Grid?
options: One share of the leftover space
why: 1fr 1fr splits space evenly; 2fr 1fr gives the first twice as much.

q: What does repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr)) achieve?
options: As many columns as fit, each at least 200px, sharing the space
why: A responsive grid with NO media query at all.

q: Flexbox is for one dimension. Grid is for:
why: Flex for a line; Grid for a two-dimensional layout.

q: Your media queries are ignored on a phone. What is almost certainly missing?
why: Without width=device-width the phone pretends to be a 980px desktop.

q: What does 'mobile-first' mean in practice?
options: Design for phones then discard the desktop
Write the phone layout as the default, then ADD with min-width queries
why: It produces simpler CSS, and phones do the least work.

q: @media (min-width: 700px) applies when the screen is:
why: min-width means 'from this width upward'.

q: How many colons does a pseudo-ELEMENT use?
why: ::before and ::after are parts; :hover and :focus are states.

q: p::before does nothing. What is missing?
why: ::before and ::after require content, even if it is empty quotes.

q: Why must you keep a visible :focus style?
options: Keyboard users cannot otherwise see where they are
why: Removing outlines with nothing to replace them is a real accessibility failure - and your syllabus names focus styles.

q: Where should the transition property be written?
why: On :hover only, the effect eases IN and snaps back OUT.

q: Which selects every second list item?
why: nth-child accepts odd, even or a formula such as 2n+1.

q: Where must CSS variables be declared to be available everywhere?
why: :root is the html element, so every rule can see them.

q: How do you USE a custom property named --brand?
why: var(--brand), with a fallback like var(--brand, #333) if you wish.

q: Which pair defines an animation?
why: @keyframes defines the steps; animation applies them.

q: Which selector targets inputs of type email?
why: Square brackets make an attribute selector.

q: a[href^="https"] selects links whose href:
why: ^= starts with, $= ends with, *= contains.
